## Today's Question

How do we repeat a tested analysis without losing track of what ran, what
failed, and what the results should look like?

## Week 12 Plan

- Meeting 1: vectorization and typed iteration
- Meeting 2: repeated workflows and failure logs
- Project 2 training package released

## Week 12 Boundary

Repeat descriptive workflows across known inputs.

Statistical models begin in Week 13.

## Meeting 1 Setup

```r
library(dplyr)
data <- airquality |>
  mutate(day_id = row_number())
```

One row is one daily observation. There are 153 rows.

Run the examples in order. The complete [worked script](../code/r/solutions/week12-vectorized-iteration_sol.R)
is available for comparison after an attempt.

## Vectorize Elementwise Work

```r
temperature_c <-
  (data$Temp - 32) * 5 / 9
```

The formula produces one Celsius value per input temperature, in the same order.
For the first observation, 67 F becomes approximately 19.44 C.

## Check The Vector Contract

```r
stopifnot(
  length(temperature_c) ==
    nrow(data),
  abs(temperature_c[1] - (67 - 32) * 5 / 9) < 1e-10,
  !any(is.na(temperature_c))
)
```

Length checks the number of results. The hand calculation checks one converted
value. Neither check proves every possible property of the data.

## What Is Being Repeated?

- Elementwise formula: operate on a vector
- Same workflow for several inputs: iterate
- Several dependent steps: a loop may be clearest

## Declare The Inputs

```r
variables <- c(
  "Ozone", "Solar.R",
  "Wind", "Temp"
)
```

Order is part of the batch contract.

## Select By A Stored Name

```r
variable_name <- "Ozone"
values <- data[[variable_name]]
```

`values` contains 153 ozone measurements, including 37 missing values.

`data[[variable_name]]` uses the stored name. `data$variable_name` looks for a
column literally named `variable_name`.

## One Summary's Contract {.smaller}

`summarize_numeric(data, variable_name)` accepts a data frame and one column name.

- The selected column must be numeric and contain an observed value.
- Missing measurements are counted and omitted from the mean and standard deviation.
- One call returns one row describing the selected variable.
- An absent column, a text column or an all-missing column causes an error.

The output has five columns: `variable`, `n_total`, `n_missing`, `mean` and
`standard_deviation`.

## Define The Summary Function {.smaller}

```r
summarize_numeric <- function(data, variable_name) {
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) stop("data must be a data frame")
  if (!is.character(variable_name) || length(variable_name) != 1)
    stop("variable_name must be one character value")
  if (!variable_name %in% names(data))
    stop("requested variable is not present")
  values <- data[[variable_name]]
  if (!is.numeric(values)) stop("requested variable must be numeric")
  observed <- values[!is.na(values)]
  if (length(observed) == 0)
    stop("requested variable has no observed values")
  tibble(
    variable = variable_name, n_total = length(values),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(values)), mean = mean(observed),
    standard_deviation = sd(observed)
  )
}
```

Read the input checks and returned row before calling the function.

## Trust One Unit First

```r
one <- summarize_numeric(data, "Ozone")
one
```

Expected: one row, `n_total = 153`, `n_missing = 37`, and `mean` approximately
42.12931. The mean uses 116 observed values.

```r
stopifnot(one$n_total == 153, one$n_missing == 37,
          abs(one$mean - 42.1293103448276) < 1e-10)
```

## `lapply`: One Object Per Input

```r
results <- lapply(
  variables,
  function(name) {
    summarize_numeric(data, name)
  }
)
```

Four column names produce four function calls. Each list element is a one-row
table, not an individual daily observation.

## The List Contract

```r
stopifnot(
  length(results) == length(variables)
)
results[[1]]
```

Inspect one element before combining.

## Combine Compatible Results

```r
summary_table <- bind_rows(results)
summary_table
stopifnot(
  nrow(summary_table) == 4,
  identical(summary_table$variable, variables),
  identical(summary_table$n_missing, c(37L, 7L, 0L, 0L))
)
```

The four rows represent Ozone, Solar.R, Wind and Temp, in that order. Compatible
columns and types allow the one-row results to be combined.

## `vapply`: State The Type

```r
means <- vapply(
  variables,
  function(name) mean(
    data[[name]], na.rm = TRUE
  ),
  numeric(1)
)
means
```

Expected means: approximately `42.1293`, `185.9315`, `9.9575`, `77.8824`.
They have different measurement units.

## Output Template

`numeric(1)` means:

- exactly one result per input
- every result numeric
- stop on the wrong shape or type

It does not prove the calculation is correct. A wrong formula can still return
one number, so retain known-answer checks.

## One Integer Count Per Column

```r
missing_counts <- vapply(
  variables,
  function(name) sum(is.na(data[[name]])),
  integer(1)
)
stopifnot(
  identical(names(missing_counts), variables),
  identical(unname(missing_counts), c(37L, 7L, 0L, 0L))
)
```

The template describes one call's result. The complete output contains four
named integer counts.

## Preallocate A Loop Result

```r
means_loop <- setNames(
  numeric(length(variables)),
  variables
)
```

The result contract exists before iteration.

## An Explicit Loop

```r
for (name in variables) {
  means_loop[[name]] <- mean(
    data[[name]], na.rm = TRUE
  )
}
```

## Compare Behavior

```r
stopifnot(
  identical(names(means), variables),
  isTRUE(all.equal(means, means_loop))
)
```

Check values, names and order. Allocating four slots does not prove all four
calculations ran.

## Choose For Clarity

- Vectorize natural elementwise operations.
- Use `vapply` for typed scalar results.
- Use `lapply` for result objects.
- Use a loop when explicit steps are clearer.

## Meeting 2 Question

When one repeated task fails, how do we keep the failure visible without
losing successful work?

## Meeting 2 Setup

Start a fresh script with:

```r
library(dplyr)
data <- airquality |>
  mutate(month_label = month.abb[Month])
```

The character column `month_label` gives us a deliberate invalid input for a
numeric summary. Define the function on the next slide before calling it.

The complete [repeated-workflow script](../code/r/solutions/week12-repeated-workflow_sol.R)
provides the matching setup and definitions.

## Define A Summary With Status {.smaller}

```r
summarize_numeric <- function(data, variable_name) {
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) stop("data must be a data frame")
  if (!is.character(variable_name) || length(variable_name) != 1)
    stop("variable_name must be one character value")
  if (!variable_name %in% names(data))
    stop("requested variable is not present")
  values <- data[[variable_name]]
  if (!is.numeric(values)) stop("requested variable must be numeric")
  if (all(is.na(values)))
    stop("requested variable has no observed values")
  tibble(
    variable = variable_name, status = "ok",
    n_total = length(values), n_missing = sum(is.na(values)),
    mean = mean(values, na.rm = TRUE),
    error_message = NA_character_
  )
}
```

## The Successful Row

```r
summarize_numeric(data, "Ozone")
```

This version returns six columns. It adds `status = "ok"` and a missing error
message (`NA_character_`), and omits the earlier standard-deviation column.

Expected: total 153, missing 37 and mean approximately 42.12931. Missing
measurements are handled by the summary's rule and do not make this call fail.

## Include Expected Failures

```r
requested_variables <- c(
  "Ozone", "month_label",
  "not_a_column", "Temp"
)
```

Expected statuses: `ok`, `error`, `error`, `ok`.

`month_label` exists but is text. `not_a_column` does not exist. Each error must
remain distinguishable from an allowed missing measurement.

## Failure Is A Result

A batch should either:

- stop clearly at the failed request; or
- retain a typed status row for that request.

It must not pretend the request never existed.

## Dangerous Shortcut

```r
generated_results <- bind_rows(lapply(
  requested_variables,
  function(name) {
    tryCatch(
      summarize_numeric(data, name),
      error = function(error) NULL
    )
  }
))
```

Expected: only Ozone and Temp remain. `bind_rows` drops the `NULL` entries,
including the identities and reasons for the two failures.

## Two Rows Cannot Describe Four Requests

```r
length(requested_variables)  # 4 requested
nrow(generated_results)     # 2 returned
generated_results$variable  # Ozone, Temp
```

The batch finished, but its output omits attempted work. We need a record for
every request before deciding which successful results to use.

## Return A Typed Error Row

```r
safe_summarize_numeric <- function(data, variable_name) {
  tryCatch(
    summarize_numeric(data, variable_name),
    error = function(error) {
      tibble(
        variable = variable_name, status = "error",
        n_total = NA_integer_, n_missing = NA_integer_,
        mean = NA_real_,
        error_message = conditionMessage(error)
      )
    }
  )
}
```

The error row matches the success row's six columns and types. `NA_real_`
means no computed numerical result, not a measured zero.

## Build The Complete Run Log

```r
run_log <- bind_rows(lapply(
  requested_variables,
  function(name) safe_summarize_numeric(data, name)
))
run_log
```

Expected: four rows in the requested order, with two successes and two readable
error messages. This wrapper captures errors. Warnings require separate review.

## The Count Exposes It

```r
stopifnot(nrow(run_log) == length(requested_variables))
```

Count reconciliation detects omitted requests. Names, order, status and type
checks establish additional parts of the contract.

## Check The Batch Log

```r
stopifnot(
  identical(run_log$variable, requested_variables),
  identical(run_log$status, c("ok", "error", "error", "ok")),
  is.double(run_log$mean),
  all(nchar(run_log$error_message[run_log$status == "error"]) > 0)
)
```

## Keep The Complete Log

```r
successful <- run_log |>
  filter(status == "ok")
```

Use successes downstream; retain `run_log` as evidence.

## Type Coercion Trap

```r
generated_mixed <- sapply(requested_variables, function(name) {
  tryCatch(
    summarize_numeric(data, name)$mean,
    error = function(error) conditionMessage(error)
  )
})
typeof(generated_mixed)  # "character"
```

All four requests remain, but combining numbers and error text turns every
entry into text. The typed status table keeps numeric results numeric.

## AI Batch Audit

- Same number of requests and records?
- Names and order preserved?
- Errors visible, and warnings reviewed?
- Numeric results still numeric?
- Stable columns and types?

## Before A Batch

- Test one valid input.
- Test one invalid input.
- Declare all requested inputs.
- State expected output count.
- State result types.

## After A Batch

- Reconcile input and output counts.
- Check names and order.
- Count successes and failures.
- Inspect types.
- Retain the complete log.
